title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How BMW Salary Sacrifice Affects Your Take-Home Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using a 38-hour week. Understand tax, super, and how BMW salary sacrifice can change your figures. Free calculator.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How is super calculated in the annual estimate?
faqs.a: Superannuation is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. The estimate stops at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator does not deduct super from your pay; it shows the employer contribution separately.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, the simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week, and that is the standard assumption here. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year.

This formula works for any hourly rate, but it assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It also assumes you do not have a salary packaging arrangement such as a **BMW salary sacrifice** – that would reduce your taxable income and change your take-home pay. The [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading, but it does not account for salary sacrifice.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To get your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same $30 per hour example: weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140; fortnightly is $2,280. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Casual employees get an extra 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Many industry awards set higher minimum rates. If you are covered by an award, check the [pay guides](/blog) for your classification.

When using the [the timesheet](/) calculator, you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator adds it for you.

## Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is the starting point for tax. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Most residents also pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page explains how to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross salary. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra amount paid into your super fund. The maximum earnings that attract the super guarantee is $270,830 per year (the maximum contribution base). If your annual pay exceeds that, super is capped.

For example, on a $60,000 salary, the employer adds $7,200 in super (12% of $60,000). Your total remuneration is $67,200, but your take-home pay is based on the $60,000 before tax.

## Salary Packaging and BMW Salary Sacrifice

Some employers offer salary packaging, including the option to sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary for a car – such as a **BMW salary sacrifice** arrangement. This reduces your taxable income, which can lower the tax you pay. However, it also reduces your super guarantee base (if the sacrifice is for a car) and may affect your entitlement to certain government benefits. The annual estimate on this site does not include salary sacrifice. If you have a BMW salary sacrifice, you should calculate your gross pay before the sacrifice and then adjust for the reduced taxable income.

## Average Earnings Context

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, in May 2026, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. That equates to about $108,352 per year for a 38-hour week. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 per year. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. For your own occupation, check the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page or industry data.

## Using the Calculator

The [the timesheet](/) page is your starting point. Enter your base hourly rate (before any casual loading). If you are casual, tick the checkbox for 25% loading. The calculator shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. It also estimates tax and super using the figures above. Remember: this is an estimate, not a binding determination.

For more detailed reference tables, see the [reference tables](/data) page. If you need to compare your rate to award minimums, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest figures.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
